The comms officer checks another screen. "There isn't a main server room in the central complex. The servers must be somewhere else in the region, probably heavily shielded. Some pre-Collapse facilities isolated their networks like that for experimental processors or advanced AI work. It kept the processors from frying the local networks or an AI from escaping into them."

He brings up the completed lidar scans. A row of giant parabolic dishes stands outside the facility. "Those are the relay dishes. You have to crank them into position by hand. That gave the staff control over when data could pass between the servers and the rest of the facility. They're all badly misaligned. We'll need to aim them ourselves."

You watch the team uncover the metal shielding and the bunker ports that receive and transmit the relay signals. Security is surprisingly light, and the salvage team reaches the central data room without much trouble. Beyond the servers, they find rooms full of Domain-era technology, archived and preserved for long-term storage. You wonder how long it would have taken anyone to stumble across the place by accident.

As you approach the entrance, you take note of the surprisingly robust infrastructure. Many of the facility systems are still operational, and the walls thrum with energy. text:

Its architecture was riddled with quantum cryptographic subsystems — designed not to think, but to crack."

text:
"Aye $playerSirOrMadam. Commencing full-spectrum sweep." Your Sensors officer acknowledges, voice steady but hands moving with grim certainty, overriding safety interlocks one by one.

The $shipOrFleet glows on the central display, its signature flaring brighter with every passing second. Amber turns to white-hot as sensor arrays flood hyperspace with precision pulses, targeting every distorted ripple, every erratic fracture along the drive-bubble sheath.

For a brief, deceptive moment, the bridge feels calm — controlled. Protocol followed, procedure executed.

Then the shift comes — imperceptible at first, a thickening of space, a low groan from the inertial compensators. Fissures bloom across the void in malignant red. Power surges climb unchecked. Alarms blink not in warning, but in confirmation.

Beyond the veil, something notices. Hunger stirs, drawn not by accident, but by deliberate signal — the irresistible lure of prey that screams its presence into the dark.

This was a mistake. A choice made by those who should have known better.

And now it comes — tendrils, maws, and seething forms pressing eagerly through widening rifts, answering a call they were never meant to hear.

"Aye $playerSirOrMadam! Executing." Your Sensors officer barks, then deftly executes a series of overrides. 

Your $shipOrFleet status is up on the central display - shield bubble an unsteady amber, incursions of N-space fissures marked in garish red. A blink of white as active sensors trigger and-

-pressure on the drive bubble spikes, an amber flash, a cacophony of alarms...

* * *

A hidden blackness waiting, lurking, jolts awake. Tendrils lunge eagerly, hungrily, through fissures in the dark behind the night.

At your command, the unperceived chorus of a multitude of ship systems and machinery dies down with a deepening sigh into muted quietude.

All that remains is the breath and bodies of your bridge's crew, a strange assertion of your shared humanity. 

Backup e-lighting, simple chemical things, provide an eerie glow. A series of dimly pulsing commands illuminate your executive interface - a flock of ardent subsystems ready to awaken from minimum operation at your touch.

* * *

A hidden blackness feels the brush of a shadow. Less than a morsel, unworthy of wakefulness. By some analog of distributed instinct a few listless tendrils explore this disturbance, this ripple in the darkness behind the night.

You wait.

Alarms are reset, battle restraints engaged. Activity on the bridge gradually quiets as all officers, crew, and systems reach a state of readiness, even anticipation - fight or flight.

The incursions crawl closer to the center of your display volume, expanding unwaveringly and intentionally. 

All eyes are on the command interfaces, and all attention is on your next order.

"Not sure, $playerSirOrMadam." The salvager shrugs. "Some of my crew are still digging through what we think is an admin wing, but somebody scrambled the database a long time ago."

You pass a military checkpoint. Beneath a broken window lies a man in a spacesuit, face up, a kinetic sniper rifle beside him. Several toxic grenades on his belt are a very particular shade of yellow. The suit has preserved him remarkably well. You can still make out the scar below his right eye.

"Likely died fighting someone up in the watchtower," one of your guards says. "Can't tell if the fall killed him or if he fell through already dead."
options: 0:aotdSpyRifle:Let's keep moving. Have someone secure the rifle and take it to the fleet armory.

text:
The salvager motions to one of his crew and leads you on. The next body wears the remnants of a long white medical coat. Its right arm is out of its socket and its rib cage has been shattered.

"Another melee kill," a guard says. "Feels like this place got infiltrated by somebody good. Somebody nobody suspected."

A few minutes later, your lights pick out a hardhat on the floor. Its owner lies sprawled beside it with a single bullet wound between his eyes.
"Poor bastard was just a systems engineer," the salvager says. "Augmented and probably dangerous, sure, but he didn't see it coming. And that hardhat was most definitely not ballistics grade."
options: 0:aotdSpyContinue:We're almost there, right? Let's get going.

text: The salvager nods. At the end of the corridor a metal door lies on the floor in two pieces. Someone went to considerable trouble to get through it. It looks kind of sad now.
"Right there, $playerSirOrMadam." Beyond the broken door he points to a frankly comically large vault door. There are more bodies between you and it.
options: 0:aotdSpyBodies:Maybe we'll find out how this story ends.

text:
You take the lead. Three bodies lie around a control panel. Their weapons are still where they fell, under the same dust that covers everything else.

The largest man is bigger than your guards in their heavy power armor, though all he wore was a light armored suit. Beside him lies a gun you know takes power assistance to lift. A mono-edge knife is buried where his spine meets his shoulder blades. He would have died instantly.

The smallest of the three is missing his head. The wall behind him is spattered with dried blood and shrapnel. His wristwatch is burnt out. Beside him lies a shattered case of narcotic inhalers with a device you don't recognize nestled among them.

The last man, head shaved, lies face down over a combat shotgun. There's a knife wound at the base of his neck. You look back at the wall. Whoever killed these two did it after they'd killed their colleague. Painfully, at that.

You step past them to the vault keypad.

text:
The keypad beeps. The four ones give way to UNLOCKED. As the vault door rolls aside, your lights fall on stacks of databanks and Domain equipment. On a wooden desk sits a blue briefcase with another keypad.

Out of curiosity, you try the same code. The latches click open.

"Whatcha find, boss?" the lead salvager asks over your shoulder.

You lift the lid.
There's an impression in the lining where something once lay. Whatever was important enough to keep in this briefcase, behind this vault door, somebody got to it first.

The keypad's beeps distort and fizzle out. Somewhere inside the door a bolt draws back. You never do learn the code.

Beyond the door lies a trove of databanks and Domain equipment. A blue briefcase sits on a wooden desk. Whoever was here last left it open. You walk over and look inside. Empty.
options: 0:aotdSpyBets:Our mystery figure was after the contents. We didn't find their body. They must have gotten out.

text:
There's a general grumbling among your guards. Credit chips quietly change hands, leaving a few of them a little richer.

The open briefcase once held something important. The mystery figure got ahold of it long before you arrived. What was in it that drove someone to commit such a massacre? You feel like you'll never know.

A few minutes later, the salvager calls you over to a combat drone replicator. Someone seems to have tried to make it mobile. Half-assembled tracks hang from its sides, and the whole thing is slathered in blue paint.
options: 0:aotdSpyTracks:What in the name of Ludd did they do to this thing?

text:
"Hell if I know," the man says, scratching his head. "Notice the bots scattered around it?"

You nudge one of the larger ones you can move yourself. It is very much a machine, but there is something familiar about the set of its shoulders.
options: 0:aotdSpyHardhat:Doesn't it look like our giant friend over there?

text:
The man crouches down and lifts its head with some effort. "Yeah, it does." He points to another bot. Its yellow head looks remarkably like a hardhat. "And that one looks like the poor bastard we found earlier."

You glance back at the machine. Beneath a patch of flaking blue paint, four stamped letters show through: MANN.

"What the hell is MANN?"

Scans of the world show an old Domain-era reactor platform half-submerged beneath the waves. A trail of slag pollutes the waters around it, leaking enough radiation for your ship's sensors to pick up.

The platform's unusual design draws the interest of your head engineer. "Before its failure and collapse, a platform like that would have supported planetary-scale logistics on a water world. If we learned more about its design, we could reverse-engineer it for use on other ocean worlds."

He recommends sending a salvage team to examine the platform, though he warns that radiation exposure may pose a risk.

text:
As the shuttle descends onto the platform, the salvage team prepares for a high-radiation environment. The dilapidated structure has left most of its security systems defunct. Through a camera feed, you watch your team make their way to the control room.

The chief salvager pings your TriPad. "I think the scans show the problem. We're in the control room, and right below us is a submerged reactor. Looks like the facility used neutrino rods for power, and they're still active."

0:aotdReactorExplain:Are the rods still radioactive?
1:aotdReactorPlay:Start the rod operation
100:defaultLeave:Leave for now

text:
"That they are," the head salvager replies. "An impact probably tore through the platform and let saltwater into the reactor room. The sodium corroded the boron control rods, and the radiation fried most of the controls."

"We need to raise the neutrino rods and sheath them. The hydraulic clamps are damaged. If we pull the rods in the wrong order, some will drop back down and damage the facility. The water will start rising as soon as I start the control panel. If it reaches the data room, we'll lose the platform designs."

With a sigh of relief, you watch the last rod rise into its lead casing. The head salvager gives you an okay through the camera feed while the team pats each other on the back. "Well done, captain. We're ready to begin salvage when you are."

You wince as the battered neutrino rod slides into its lead casing. The hydraulics shudder with a groan as saltwater seeps into the room.

"Looks like the facility took a hit, but the damage seems manageable," the head salvager reports. "We're ready to proceed with salvage when you are."

The head salvager shakes his head. "That went badly, captain. We'll see what can still be recovered in the remaining rooms."
